title: "The Modeler's Bench"
subtitle: "One drug, many models"
toc: false
---

An open, reproducible curriculum for quantitative pharmacology.

Learn by rebuilding the same set of decisions about the same molecules — in the
tools a sponsor would actually use, with data whose **true parameters are
published**, so you can find out exactly how far your answer landed from the
truth. No course built on real data can do that.

Everything here is free, the code runs, and every notebook is re-executed on
every change so it does not quietly rot.

## Pick a path

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [A · The New Modeler](paths/path-a-new-modeler.qmd)
Junior industry scientist with a deliverable due.

*Your first defensible population PK analysis in eight weeks.* Workflow, data
assembly, diagnostics, and how the result gets used. Ends at a written report,
not a converged run.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [B · The Trainee](paths/path-b-trainee.qmd)
Graduate student, postdoc, academic modeler.

*From ODEs to a model you can defend in a viva.* Theory, estimation mechanics,
identifiability and uncertainty. Ends at a reproducible, citable analysis.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [C · The Crossover](paths/path-c-crossover.qmd)
Bench pharmacologist, clinician, DMPK, statistician, data scientist.

*Read a modeling report without bluffing.* Interpretation and vocabulary first,
then branch deeper — or stop satisfied. Both are wins.
:::

:::

## Or start at the beginning

[**S0-00 · What quantitative pharmacology is, and how to become one**](lessons/s0-00-what-is-qp/index.qmd)
— the field, the job, the skill ladder, and a concrete twelve-month route in.

**No pharmacology background?** Start with
[**Strand P · Pharmacology from the beginning**](pharmacology.qmd) — eighteen
lessons that assume nothing, written for people arriving from statistics,
mathematics, engineering or software.

**Working in one disease?** [**Strand D · Disease areas**](diseases.qmd) is where
biology stops being general and starts changing model structure. First up:
pancreatic cancer.

**Want to see the arguments that actually got made?** [**Strand C · Approved
drugs**](drugs.qmd) reads the clinical pharmacology of twelve FDA-approved
products out of the public-domain review record — including one regimen approved
with no new efficacy trial, and one product whose review contains no clinical
pharmacology at all.

## Two reference pages, both free to use

[**Reading**](reading.qmd) — 94 papers, every one verified against PubMed, with
a one-line note on what it is actually for and an honest statement of which we
have read in full.

[**Resources**](resources.qmd) — 249 software packages, courses, regulatory
guidances, model repositories, reference databases and FDA approval packages.
**Every URL was fetched and checked**, and the cost and licence of each was read
off the page rather than recalled. 219 of the 249 are usable at no cost, and the
page has a free-only filter for exactly that reason.

development decision it serves before it teaches anything.

## How a lesson is built

Seven slots, every time:

1. **The decision it serves** — one sentence. If it cannot be written, the lesson does not exist yet.
2. **Concept** — 800–1,200 words, one figure, no derivation for its own sake.
3. **Runnable notebook** — open tools, real case data, executed in CI.
4. **Rosetta panel** — the same thing in a second language or engine.
5. **Failure mode** — broken on purpose, with the diagnostic that catches it.
6. **Self-check** — three questions, folded answers.
7. **Discussion and citations** — a thread per lesson, and where this shows up in practice.

## The cases

Four fictional molecules carried through every strand, each simulated from a
documented generative model published alongside the data. See
[Cases](cases.qmd) — [`CASE-SM` "Ozanib"](cases.qmd#case-sm) is live and used
throughout `S0`.
